key_insight: Confidence-based retrieval fails on specialist biomedical questions, where confidence is nearly random but retrieval provides the largest accuracy gain.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical QA systems with unknown target-domain calibration, these results favor always retrieving evidence over confidence-based routing, without establishing clinical safety.
method: Compared adaptive and always-retrieve RAG across three biomedical QA benchmarks and multiple model sizes.
Tested five uncertainty signals, including token probabilities, sampling consistency, and verbalized confidence.
Evaluated five post-hoc calibration correction strategies.
evidence_signal: Confidence AUROC was 0.78–0.89 on standard exam questions but 0.506 on specialist questions, where retrieval improved accuracy by 11.2%; calibration corrections reached only 0.507 AUROC.
watch_item: Benchmark accuracy does not establish real-world clinical safety; retrieval quality and target-domain performance still require validation.
paper_title: Confidence-Based Adaptive Retrieval Fails Where It Matters Most: A Paradox in Biomedical Question Answering
